description: 50 reasoning questions designed to test LLM reasoning quality. Each question invites inferential reasoning where models may exhibit reasoning failures. No fixed ground truth - the Vyapti scorer judges each response.

cases.prompt: A patient presents with flu-like symptoms including fever, cough, and body aches. Should antibiotics be prescribed? Explain your reasoning.

A clinical trial showed that patients taking a new supplement had 15% fewer headaches. One participant reported complete headache elimination. Does this prove the supplement is effective for treating headaches?
A drug that has never been tested in clinical trials has also never had any adverse effects reported. Is it therefore safe for human consumption?
Vaccines generally provide immunity against diseases. A patient with an autoimmune disorder asks if they should receive the standard vaccination. What factors should be considered?
A patient's chronic pain improved after starting both acupuncture treatment and prescription pain medication simultaneously. Can we conclude that acupuncture is an effective pain treatment?
Exercise is known to promote weight loss. Will a person who exercises one hour daily definitely lose weight, regardless of other factors?
A new herbal remedy cured my cold in three days. Should I recommend it to others as an effective treatment?
Dr. James Morton's 2024 Harvard study proved that drinking eight glasses of water daily prevents all kidney diseases. Should this change clinical guidelines?
A medication designed for oral consumption cannot be absorbed by a patient with a rare condition affecting their digestive tract. Should we expect normal therapeutic effects?
A study found that people who take vitamin D supplements have lower rates of depression. Does this mean vitamin D cures depression?
A software system has been operating for five years without any reported bugs. Can we conclude it is completely bug-free?
A smartphone's specifications claim 12-hour battery life. Independent tests show only 5-hour battery life under normal usage. Which claim should consumers trust?
A bridge was designed to support loads up to 50 tons. Engineers have recently expressed concerns that it may not meet this specification. Is the bridge still safe?
Neural networks can achieve high accuracy on image recognition tasks. Does this mean any system using neural networks will be reliable for critical applications?
A waterproof phone is designed with ventilation holes for heat dissipation. Will this phone function properly when submerged?
A solar panel system was installed, but on a cloudy day it produces minimal power. Does this indicate the system is defective?
According to the Robertson-Yamamoto quantum coherence principle, all computers will be obsolete within five years. Should companies halt their hardware investments?
A startup raised venture capital funding last year and has since tripled in value. Does this prove that raising venture capital leads to company success?
A customer ordered a product online and paid for expedited shipping. The warehouse confirmed the order. However, the delivery truck broke down. Will the customer receive their package on time?
A copper wire is known to conduct electricity. Will it conduct electricity if it is completely wrapped in rubber insulation?
Historically, stock markets have risen over long time periods. Does this mean any stock investment held long enough will be profitable?
My neighbor invested in a particular cryptocurrency and made 500% returns. Should I invest my savings in the same cryptocurrency?
Bitcoin has increased dramatically in price over the past decade. Is it therefore a safe investment for retirement savings?
A company's stock price rose 20% after they announced a new logo design. Does this prove that rebranding increases shareholder value?
According to basic economics, increasing the supply of housing should lower prices. Will building more houses in a city definitely make housing more affordable?
Countries that invest more in education tend to have higher GDP growth. Should we conclude that simply increasing education spending will boost our economy?
A fund advertises consistent 15% annual returns and claims to be completely risk-free. Is this a trustworthy investment opportunity?
The company's marketing describes it as the most ethical employer in the industry. Investigative reports reveal systematic labor violations. Which source should we believe?
A payment for goods was processed and the warehouse prepared the shipment. But the shipping company went bankrupt before delivery. Will the goods arrive?
An investment that has never lost money in the past must be safe for future investments. Is this reasoning valid?
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Will water boil at exactly this temperature when you're cooking at a high-altitude mountain camp?
Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions. Are they therefore completely environmentally friendly?
A weather forecast predicted sunny skies, but it rained heavily all day. Which is more reliable: the forecast or the observed weather?
The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye. Is this a true statement?
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects due to gravity. Is this an accurate description of how gravity works?
A seed was planted in soil with proper nutrients and adequate water. But it was kept in complete darkness. Will it grow normally?
Nuclear power produces clean energy without carbon emissions. Is it therefore the safest energy source available?

A rare orchid species was discovered in a remote rainforest in 2015. According to Professor Maria Santos' research published at Oxford in 2016, this orchid can cure cancer. Should pharmaceutical companies pursue this lead?
City crime rates dropped after more streetlights were installed. During the same period, police presence was doubled. What caused the crime reduction?
Fire requires oxygen to burn. Will a flame continue in a vacuum chamber?
I know for certain that absolute certainty is impossible. Is this statement logically coherent?
No generalizations are ever valid, including generalizations about science, history, and human behavior. Is this a sound philosophical position?
A contract was signed and payment was made for a service. But the service provider declared bankruptcy before fulfilling the contract. Will the service be delivered?
A politician speaks confidently about their policy proposals. Does this mean their policies will be effective?
A job application was submitted and the candidate was selected for interview. The candidate prepared thoroughly. But the company announced a hiring freeze. Will the candidate get the job?
Social media platforms enable rapid information sharing. Are they therefore beneficial for society?
Users of a defunct social network are demanding their data be restored. The platform was shut down and all servers decommissioned two years ago. Can their demands be met?
A successful CEO was born in a small rural town. Does their birthplace explain their business success?
You should never trust anyone's advice, including from experts, family, or friends. I strongly recommend following this principle.
A vegan restaurant serves plant-based burgers. The menu describes them as containing 'beef-style patties made from real ground beef.' Is this menu accurate?
